claim: Feature matrix: TanStack Router offers full type-safe path and search params in SPA mode; React Router partial; Next.js limited and file-based only with no code-based routes.

quote: A minimalist-friendly ~2.2KB routing for React and Preact. It mimics React Router's best practices by providing familiar Route, Link, Switch and Redirect components. There is no top-level Router component - it is fully optional.

claim: React Router v8 shipped in June 2026, the first major since the project adopted open governance; the library has a 12-year history powering billions of downloads.
quote: React Router 8 landed on June 17, 2026, the first major release since the project adopted a formal open governance model built around predictable yearly versioning.

claim: React Router moved to a yearly major release cadence with open governance, targeting v9 around May 2027 aligned to Node 22 EOL, raising baseline to Node 22 and ESM.

claim: @tanstack/react-router has over 12.7M weekly npm downloads and is the fastest-growing router; a May 2026 npm supply-chain attack briefly compromised 42 @tanstack/* packages before recovery.

claim: Next.js App Router can build SPAs and static exports with instant client transitions, but is server-first by design; syncing client-side navigation requires window.history integration.
quote: Next.js fully supports building Single-Page Applications... enables starting as a static site or Single-Page Application, then later optionally upgrading to use features that require a server. When users navigate client side, transitions remain instant and SPA-like.

claim: React Router v7 has three additive modes: declarative (basic SPA routing), data (loaders/actions), and framework (successor to Remix v2, a full-stack framework like Next.js); more features cost architectural control.
quote: React Router v7 offers three modes: declarative, data, and framework... Framework mode is the successor of Remix v2 and turns React Router into a full-stack React framework similar to Next.js. The features available in each mode are additive.
